In mathematics, a '''Brieskorn manifold''' or '''Brieskorn–Phạm manifold''',  introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Brieskorn|first=Egbert|authorlink=Egbert Brieskorn|year=1966|year2=1966b}}, is the intersection of a small sphere around the origin with the singular, complex hypersurface
:<math>x_1^{k_1}+\cdots+x_n^{k_n}=0</math>
studied by {{harvs|txt|last=Pham|first=Frédéric|authorlink=Frédéric Pham|year=1965}}.

Brieskorn manifolds give examples of [[exotic sphere]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Greuel |first1=Gert-Martin |last2=Purkert |first2=Walter |author-link2=Walter Purkert|year=2018 |title=Life and work of Egbert Brieskorn (1936&ndash;2013) |url=http://www.journalofsing.org/volume18/article1.html |journal=[[Journal of Singularities]]|volume=18|pages=1–28| doi=10.5427/jsing.2018.18a|arxiv=1711.09600|MR=3899530 |doi-access=free}} (See pp. 19–23.)</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=van der Meer, J. W.|title=On the Construction and Classification of Exotic Structures on the 7-Sphere|postscript=; Bachelor's thesis|year=2017|publisher=Utrecht University|url=https://studenttheses.uu.nl/bitstream/handle/20.500.12932/26993/Bachelor%20Thesis.pdf?sequence=2}}</ref> for example the [[Gromoll–Meyer sphere]].
